text.p: The supervisory board of ailing Polish furniture producer Swarzedz SA has approved an outline of a restructuring plan for 1997-99 to be presented to the firm's creditors, the company said in a statement on Monday.

The company made a net loss of 28.5 million zlotys in September and 34.1 million zlotys over this year's first three quarters after its auditor recommended that it make large provisions for receivables.

"The supervisory board has accepted the outline of a restructuring programme and obliged the management and its financial adviser to work out a detailed operational plan and time-table," the statement said.
It said the document would be handed to the company's creditors this week as the basis for further negotiations.
Officials at Swarzedz, whose full name is Swarzedzkie Fabryki Mebli Swarzedz SA, declined to give details on the plan.
The company has said it is considering a debt-for-equity scheme to compensate the main credtors, which include Polish Development Bank (PBR), Bank Gdanski and Powszechny Bank Gospodarczy SA (PBG).
